config.faid_policy_rationale: Missing a deserving student is worse than sending an extra borderline case to committee review, so threshold selection should prioritize recall as long as shortlist quality remains operationally usable.
config.faid_policy_weight_rationale: The 3:1 weighting between missed-need errors and extra-review burden is a policy assumption that reflects committee priorities rather than an empirically learned truth. It encodes the view that excluding a deserving student is materially more harmful than reviewing one additional borderline case.
config.decision_boundary_rationale: Approve and reject actions require materially stronger confidence than the policy threshold itself, while a review band around the threshold preserves human oversight for borderline cases.
config.fairness_threshold_rationale: A 0.10 subgroup gap is used as a practical governance trigger: smaller differences are monitored, while larger differences are treated as operationally meaningful enough to override automation.
config.fairness_min_group_size_rationale: A minimum subgroup size of 30 is used to avoid overreacting to very small groups where error-rate estimates are unstable.
config.fairness_limitations_note: Fairness monitoring in this workflow is rule-based rather than causal. Group gaps should be interpreted as governance signals for review, not definitive proof of unfair treatment.
config.local_explanation_note: Local case explanations are model-native approximations unless SHAP is separately added. They are intended to improve transparency, not to claim a full causal explanation of any individual eligibility decision.

data.target_definition_note: Only explicit award and denial outcomes are used for binary training. Rows with unlabeled, ambiguous, or structurally different outcomes remain out of the training target.
data.excluded_label_rationale: Excluded labels represent programs or outcomes that are not directly comparable to the core eligibility decision, so they are removed rather than forced into the negative class.

temporal_split_assessment.note: A true temporal split is feasible using parsed_application_term grouped into application-cycle years. Training uses earlier cycles, validation uses the next cycle, and final testing uses the latest cycle.

future_deployment_validation_plan.step: Freeze one approved feature/threshold policy bundle before the next admissions cycle opens.
future_deployment_validation_plan.purpose: Prevent silent threshold or feature drift during live deployment.

future_deployment_validation_plan.step: Score the next full cycle without retraining and compare later committee outcomes against the frozen predictions.
future_deployment_validation_plan.purpose: Measure future-cycle discrimination, calibration, and operational error rates honestly.

future_deployment_validation_plan.step: Re-run fairness action rules on the future cycle before allowing any broader automation.
future_deployment_validation_plan.purpose: Ensure subgroup gaps remain governed rather than assumed stable.

future_deployment_validation_plan.step: Update the model only after documenting drift, missed-need errors, and review burden under the previous bundle.

selection_summary.strategy: Shortlist by CV ROC AUC, then validation ROC AUC, then prefer lower overfit gap and better calibration quality when differences are effectively tied.
selection_summary.selection_reason: Chosen from the near-top ROC AUC candidates because it provided the best stability/overfit trade-off on validation.

normal_workflow.threshold_policy_rationale: Missing a deserving student is worse than sending an extra borderline case to committee review, so threshold selection should prioritize recall as long as shortlist quality remains operationally usable.
